Suggest a confidence threshold per species

Source: R/post_validation.R
suggest_thresholds.Rd

For each site and species (and each level of the by columns), the lowest confidence c such that the precision among the reviewed clips with confidence >= c reaches target_precision, with at least min_n clips. Candidate cuts are the observed confidences rounded to two decimals.

Usage

suggest_thresholds(
  validation,
  target_precision = 0.9,
  min_n = 15,
  by = NULL,
  weighted = NULL,
  sustained = FALSE
)

Arguments

validation

Table returned by classify_review().

target_precision

Target precision.

min_n

Minimum of reviewed clips for a bin to be taken seriously; bins with fewer are flagged in low_support.

by

Optional columns of validation that split each site x species cell further, e.g. the bin of an environmental gradient or of an acoustic index joined from covariate_bins(). They show which parts of the gradient lack reviewed clips.

weighted

Which precision chooses the cut. NULL (default): the weighted one in the cells whose clips all have inclusion_prob, the unweighted one elsewhere. TRUE: always the weighted one; cells with clips without inclusion_prob get no threshold, with a warning, and it is an error if no clip has it. FALSE: always the unweighted one, and n_support for min_n.

sustained

Must the target also hold at every higher cut with at least min_n clips? See Sustained target.

Value

A tibble with site, species_folder, the by columns, threshold, n_support, precision_at_threshold (unweighted; NA when no cut reaches the target). With inclusion_prob, also precision_weighted_at_threshold, n_eff (Kish's effective sample size at the threshold) and precision_used ("weighted" or "unweighted", the precision that chose the cut). Without any reviewed clip with a confidence, the tibble has no rows.

Details

Sustained target. With sustained = TRUE, the target must also hold at every higher cut with at least min_n clips, the rule of calibrated_thresholds(). This is not the default: the curve of the model is smooth, while the empirical precision of a high cut rests on few clips, so a cut can fail by chance, and the failure of the highest supported cut leaves the cell without a threshold. In a simulation with 300 clips per cell, the share of cells without a threshold rose from 0.09 to 0.24, and the true precision of the cuts from 0.888 to 0.896 (dev/sustained-threshold-rule.R).

The precision is computed from the reviewed clips of each cell alone, so it is reliable only when the clips were drawn at random within the cell and are numerous. calibrated_thresholds() derives the thresholds from the calibration model of stage 2 instead.

Design weights. Clips of "random_detections" have unequal inclusion_prob: quiet strata are reviewed almost in full and choruses lightly. The plain share of positive clips then estimates the precision of the reviewed sample, not that of the predictions kept by the cut. So, by default, a cell whose clips all have inclusion_prob is judged by the precision weighted by 1 / inclusion_prob, as in precision_by_bin(), and min_n applies to Kish's effective sample size, \((\sum w)^2 / \sum w^2\), so that a cut resting on a few heavily weighted clips is not accepted. With equal inclusion probabilities, both choices give the same threshold. The weights cost variance: when precision does not vary between strata, the unweighted estimate is also unbiased and less variable (weighted = FALSE).

A cell that mixes clips with and without inclusion_prob ("top" and "random_detections", say) cannot be weighted: it gets the unweighted precision, with a warning, since "top" clips are not a probability sample and should not set thresholds.

See also

calibrated_thresholds() for thresholds from the calibration model.
